name: ma1_build_replay_day_lpc_stamping
description: MA-1 (AC-1): synthetic_history.build_replay_day already computes a per-ticker per-tick fractional return (ret = (bar['c'] - yesterday_closes[ticker]) / yesterday_closes[ticker]) for the aggregate-return sum, but never stamps it onto a holdings copy as 'last_percent_change' before calling math_engine.run_monte_carlo -- so every holding is excluded from run_monte_carlo's current_symphony_return sum (math_engine.py:1162-1166 excludes any holding whose last_percent_change is None) and the MC output is degenerate/day-constant. This fixture supplies a 5-tick canned bar series for one ticker whose close price swings well above and below yesterday's close, so the per-tick lpc the fix must stamp varies materially tick to tick.
derivation: expected_lpc = (c - yesterday_close) / yesterday_close for each tick, computed independently in the test (not read back from the producer) -- e.g. tick 1: (97.0 - 100.0) / 100.0 = -0.03. historical_data_spec uses 45 explicit, deterministically-varied (SPY, AAA) daily-return rows rather than a strict 2-value alternating pattern: an alternating pattern produces a near-zero-variance feature that trips math_engine.compute_regime_match_quality's Mahalanobis chi-squared guard inside build_replay_day (is_unprecedented=True -> mc_prob forced to None for every tick, which would make the mc-varies-across-ticks assertion vacuously fail for the WRONG reason -- verified empirically against the real functions before locking this fixture: with these rows, is_unprecedented=False and the 5 tick closes below produce 3 distinct mc_prob values once lpc is correctly wired). 45 raw days -> 26 eligible days (>= MC_MIN_HISTORY_DAYS=20) so run_monte_carlo returns a real (non-sentinel) mc_prob for every tick.
